title: Beef Rendang
subtitle: Indonesian slow-braised beef in coconut and spices
excerpt: One of the world's great spiced braises: chunks of beef simmered in coconut milk with lemongrass, galangal, and a complex spice paste for hours until the liquid has completely evaporated and the meat is coated in a thick, deeply fragrant, almost-dry coating.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rendang originated with the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra and spread throughout the Malay world: it is now considered a national dish of both Indonesia and Malaysia. The cooking method is unusual and defines the dish: beef is simmered in coconut milk with a spice paste and aromatics, but unlike a Western braise, the cooking continues until all the liquid has evaporated and the beef fries in the remaining coconut oil. The result is meat with almost no sauce, coated in a thick, caramelised layer of concentrated spice and coconut. This process can take two to three hours. Rendang improves enormously with age: stored in the fridge, it keeps for a week, and the flavour deepens. It was traditionally made in large quantities to travel with and last without refrigeration for several days.

content.text: The final stage of cooking (after all the liquid has evaporated and the meat is frying in its own coconut oil) requires careful stirring to prevent the spice coating from burning. Reduce the heat and stir frequently in the last 20 minutes. The colour should be deep brown, almost black at the edges, but not burnt.

items.preparation: cut into large chunks, about 5 cm
bashed and tied in a knot
toasted in a dry pan until golden; adds texture

content.text: Blend or pound the ginger, garlic, shallots, chilli, and shrimp paste with the ground spices to a smooth paste. Heat a large, wide pan over medium heat. Fry the paste for 5 minutes until very fragrant. Add the beef pieces and stir to coat thoroughly in the paste.

Add the coconut milk, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, toasted desiccated coconut, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a moderate simmer. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 1 hour 30 minutes until the liquid is almost gone and the mixture is thick and bubbling.

Reduce the heat to low. Continue cooking, stirring frequently, for a further 30 to 45 minutes as the coconut oil separates and the beef fries in it. The meat should be coated in a thick, dark-brown, almost-dry crust with no liquid remaining. Remove the lemongrass and lime leaves. Serve with steamed rice.
